title: Review of c29's kernel-drive ringed cells (SIBMD): replicates on fresh seed 3 (L rim/core 1.57, 220 persistent splits to generation 7, 53 ringed swimmers >= 3 BL, one track that swims 4.9 BL ringed and divides), including the jam into a static lattice by t~7000
summary: Re-ran world.py with the stated WORLD_P {drive: kernel, mu: 1.0, kd: 0.08, chi: 5} on fresh seed 3: labkit (256^2, t=10000) and c29's ringtrack.py to t=10000 with lineage_report.py (data/rt_s3.report.txt). From noise, cells with a link ring form by t~850, swim as crescents and divide while colonizing the empty space (t=850-5000); the torus fills and the cells freeze into a static lattice by t~7000 (rerun/sheet.png). labkit: L rim/core 1.57, rim/out 9.85, 920/1275 individuals membrane-like; 562 splits, 220 persistent, max generation 7, merge/split 0.21; 107 tracks >= 1 body length, max 4.3. ringtrack: ring >= 1.5 in 94.6% of 7420 cell-frames (median 1.67), 57 persistent splits, 53 tracks swim >= 3 BL and all are ringed in >= half their frames; 1 track (#18, t=1000-5120) swims 4.91 BL with ring median 1.53 and divides into #806 and #807.

observations.I: rerun/sheet.png t=850-10000: discrete walled cells at bounded size
observations.B: rerun/radial.png: L rim/core 1.57, rim/out 9.85, 920/1275 membrane-like; ringtrack ring >= 1.5 in 94.6% of cell-frames
observations.M: data/rt_s3.report.txt: 53 tracks >= 3 BL, all ringed; labkit 107 tracks >= 1 BL, max 4.3
observations.D: rerun/lineage.png: 220 persistent splits, generation 7, merge/split 0.21; data/rt_s3.report.txt: track #18 swims 4.91 BL then divides into #806/#807

seeds_run.result: pass: ring, swimming and division reproduce; one same-track swim+ring+divide lineage; jam by t~7000

verdicts.limitation: Swim-then-divide in one track is rare (1 track on seed 3, as 1-3 on the claim's seeds), and #18's daughters are too small to be ring-scored; everything happens during colonization, and from t~7000 the cells sit in a static lattice. The drive is a smoothed substrate-gradient advection written into the update (local, no labels), and the ring is chi drift up the wall indicator of the cell's own links (L3 quasi-equilibrium clause). world.py's defaults are the label drive (drive=label, mu 1.5, chi 2, kd 0.03), so the claimed world needs the WORLD_P given in the README; the pack FACTS command lines do not show it. I did not rerun the mu=0 and chi=0 controls; no dt or resolution test.
